Although Moving Out is advertised as a co-op game, it actually works very well as a single-player game too.
The only downside is that to 100% the game as a solo player, it's necessary to enable Assist Mode (just the first option that adds more time is more than enough), but luckily this doesn't forbid you to get all achievements.

These devs really thought about the single-player aspect too, and I must thank them for that. I also add that DLC levels are as good as the base game ones.

I really enjoyed this game (alone). I recommend this purchase for both single players and co-op ones.
If you're sitting on the fence, you can wait for a sale, they often heavily discount both the game and DLCs.

Moving Out turns furniture removal into physics-driven comedy, though the charming presentation only sustains the premise for a short time. Mistimed throws and cramped hallways generate genuine laughs in a full lobby, but stripping the headcount exposes how little the mechanics demand. Time limits stay generous throughout, and the Guava Run level towards the end is the only instance where co-op feels like a meaningful requirement. Bonus objectives remain hidden until a level is cleared; framed as vague hints, they provide little incentive for replay. It has a clear identity but a low ceiling, held back by a lack of mechanical challenge. While co-op is fun in small doses, it remains largely forgettable.

[b]Merits:[/b] 
▪ Cute graphics & story 
▪ Playable Co-Op & Solo 
▪ Accessibility & Assistance Options 
 
[b]Flaws:[/b] 
▪ It becomes repetitive fast 
▪ Some challenges are really frustrating 
▪ Some achievements are tied to DLC purchase 
 
[b]Verdict:[/b] 
Moving Out is similar to Overcooked, though not as involved nor as fun as the aforementioned title. I think this game is worth picking up when it goes on sale, especially if you play it with friends in couch co-op. 
 
[b]Rating:[/b] 
★★★☆☆ - Above Average
I recommend this over Overcooked as one of the top couch co-op games!
